plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn lilac as these feathery-leaved trees cover themselves in clusters of trumpet-shaped blooms. The fallen flowers carpet pavements and parked cars in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early October to November (peaking in late October and November in Sydney, and through October in Brisbane)
plants.location: Sydney and Brisbane, eastern Australia (native to South America)
plants.funFact: Native to South America, jacarandas have become a symbol of spring in Australia. Their bloom is so well loved that cities hold festivals around it.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped blooms emerge straight from bare soil, without a leaf in sight, and dot damp meadows and garden borders with soft pink and lilac. The leaves appeared months earlier and have already died away.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, typically September to October
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across temperate Europe, including Britain and central Europe
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true crocus. It belongs to the lily relatives, and its flowers are a source of colchicine, a powerful compound used in medicine and plant breeding. All parts of the plant are highly poisonous.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Daisy-like flowers with silky, notched petals sway above fine, ferny foliage on tall stems. They keep producing blooms until the first frost, which makes them a cheerful sight in October gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer until first frost, roughly July to October
plants.location: Gardens across temperate Northern Hemisphere regions (native to Mexico)
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony. It refers to the neat, balanced arrangement of the petals.
